subject: physics
title: Efficiency
key_idea: **Efficiency** is the fraction of the total input energy that is transferred usefully. Divide the useful output energy by the total input energy. It is never more than 1, or 100%. Reducing wasted energy makes a device more efficient.

blocks.text: No device is perfect. Some of the input energy is always dissipated, so the useful output is less than the input.

items.meaning: The proportion of the total input energy that is transferred usefully.
The energy transferred to the store or form you want.
Total input energy minus useful output energy.

items: Efficiency is less than 1 (100%) because some energy is transferred to less useful forms.
A more efficient device wastes less energy.
A more efficient device needs a lower energy input for the same energy output.
Efficiency compares useful output with total input.
Efficiency is always less than 1 (100%).
Wasted energy is dissipated, not destroyed.

blocks.text: You can use energy or power. The answer is the same because both have the same time.

blocks.label: Efficiency from energy
blocks.formula: efficiency = useful output energy transfer ÷ total input energy transfer
where: The answer is a decimal from 0 to 1. Multiply by 100 for a percentage.

blocks.label: Efficiency from power
blocks.formula: efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input

items.text: A cooker supplies 130 000 J, but only 96 000 J heats the milk.

blocks.text: Change the input energy and the useful output to see the efficiency and the wasted energy.

diagram.alt: Change the total input energy and the useful output energy to see the efficiency and the wasted energy.
Calculate useful output energy from an efficiency percentage and an input energy.
diagram.question: A device has an efficiency of {e}%. The total input energy is {Ein} J. Calculate the useful energy output.

blocks.text: Finding total input or wasted energy

items: Total input = useful output ÷ efficiency. A 55% efficient oven that transfers 42 000 J needs 42 000 ÷ 0.55 = 76 000 J.
Wasted energy = total input − useful output.
If energy is given in MJ, the efficiency is the same without converting to joules.
Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input, as a decimal or a percentage.
Rearrange to find the useful output or total input.
Wasted energy is the input minus the useful output.

blocks.text: To raise efficiency, reduce the energy that is wasted.

items: Lubricate moving parts to reduce friction.
Streamline vehicles to reduce drag.
Use thermal insulation to reduce unwanted heat loss.
Use thicker, low-resistance wires.
More efficient devices waste less energy.
They cost less to run and use less electricity for the same output.
Less electricity has to be generated, so there is less environmental impact, such as lower carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels.
Reduce friction, drag and unwanted heating to increase efficiency.
An efficient device needs a lower energy input for the same output.
Efficient devices cost less to run and reduce demand for electricity.

checks.q: A motor has an input energy of 1.5 MJ and its useful output is 0.6 MJ. Calculate its efficiency.
An LED has a total power input of 0.24 W and an efficiency of 0.75. Calculate the useful power output.
Explain why the efficiency of an engine is less than 1 (100%).
checks.a: The useful output energy is less than the input energy, because some energy is transferred to less useful forms, such as thermal energy.

exam_phrases: more efficient devices waste less energy
more efficient devices need a lower energy input (for the same energy output)
which would minimise the electricity / energy demand

mistakes.wrong: Efficient devices are better for the environment.
mistakes.right: Qualify it. More efficient devices waste less energy, so less electricity needs to be generated, with lower carbon dioxide emissions.
Say why. They waste less energy, or need a lower energy input for the same energy output.
Multiply the efficiency by the total power input: 0.75 × 0.24 = 0.18 W.

worked_example.question:
The total power input to an LED was 0.24 W.
The efficiency of the LED was 0.75.

Calculate the useful power output of the LED.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution, one for the rearrangement and one for the answer.

exam_phrases: (useful) output energy is less than input energy
some energy is transferred to less useful forms

mistakes.wrong: The efficiency of the cooker is 74.
mistakes.right: Give 0.74 or 74%. An answer of 74 without the % sign scores only 1 mark.
Check the power of ten. 42 000 / 0.55 = 76 000 J. A power of ten error loses marks.

mistakes.wrong: The efficiency is less than 1 because the engine destroys some of the energy.
mistakes.right: Energy is not destroyed. The useful output is less than the input because some energy is transferred to less useful forms, such as thermal energy.

worked_example.question:
A microwave oven is 55% efficient and transfers 42 000 J of energy to some food when it is heated.

Calculate the total amount of energy that must be supplied to the oven.
answer_points: Selection and substitution: (0.)55 = 42 000 / total energy supplied (to device)
worked_example.tip: Substitution and rearrangement can be in either order. Any answer that rounds to 76 000 J scores the evaluation mark.

exam_phrases: reduce the friction between the car and track / lubrication

mistakes.wrong: The energy wasted by the lamp is 4 J.
mistakes.right: 4 J is the useful energy. The wasted energy is the input minus the useful output: 10 − 4 = 6 J.

mistakes.wrong: The efficiency of the motor is 40.
mistakes.right: Give 0.4 or 40%. The answer 40 without the % sign scores only 1 mark.

mistakes.wrong: Convert 0.6 MJ and 1.5 MJ to joules before finding the efficiency.
mistakes.right: This is not needed. A ratio of two energies in the same unit gives the same efficiency: 0.6 ÷ 1.5 = 0.4.

worked_example.question:
One LED lamp has an efficiency of 0.4.
In one second, the input energy transferred by the lamp is 10 J.

Calculate the energy wasted by the lamp in one second.
Use the equation: efficiency = useful output energy transfer / input energy transfer
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 6 J scores all 3 marks. Working out only the useful energy, 4 J, scores 2 marks.
